rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun, like Pharaoh for political despotism, epitomizes financial despotism and hoarding; his story depicts a monopolist capitalist.
rows.anchor: Firavun, siyâsî zulm ü istibdadda alem olduğu gibi Kārûn da mâlî istibdad ve ihtikârda alemdir. Bu suretle Kārûn kıssası muhtekir bir kapitalist kıssasıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun was an Israelite and a relative of Moses.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın kavminden idi yani Benî İsrâil’den ve Mûsâ’nın akrabasından idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı explains Qarun's transgression as hoarding, withholding zakat, and rebelling against Moses.
rows.anchor: derken onlara karşı bağyetti ihtikâr yaptı, zekâtını vermedi, Mûsâ’ya isyan etti.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some take one's worldly share to mean lawful provision and legitimate worldly enjoyment; Elmalılı rejects that interpretation.
rows.anchor: bazıları helâl dünya rızkı ve meşrû dünya zevki diye anlamak istemişlerse de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the transient world; one's true share from it is benefit and deeds carried into the afterlife, as the world is the afterlife's cultivation.
rows.anchor: o geçici dünyanın kendisi demektir. Asıl dünyadan nasib ise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds that worldly share ultimately amounts only to a shroud, illustrating this with Persian verse about people striving for a shroud between nonexistence and existence.
rows.anchor: Yoksa dünyadan nasib nihâyet bir kefendir:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hoarding such a great treasure and trapping wealth is itself corruption.
rows.anchor: bu kadar hazineyi ihtikâr edip de serveti hapsetmek haddizâtında bir fesaddır.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some interpret Qarun's claim of knowledge as referring to his knowledge of trade and economics.
rows.anchor: bu ilme bazıları ticaret ve iktisad ilmi demişler

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Others interpret the knowledge Qarun claimed to possess as alchemy.
rows.anchor: iktisad ilmi demişler, bazıları da el-kimya demişler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if Qarun's wealth came solely from his knowledge, he should have learned that God destroyed earlier people stronger and richer than him, such as Pharaoh; why did he not benefit from that knowledge?
rows.anchor: ile olsa kurûn-ı ûlâ içinde ondan daha kuvvetli ve daha çok servetli (Firavun gibi) kimseleri helâk etmiş olduğunu bilmiyor muydu?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals need not be questioned to establish their guilt: God knows them, and angels recognize them by their faces and seize them immediately, as 55:41 says.
rows.anchor: meleklerce de sîmalarından bilinir ve derhâl yaka paça tutulurlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awthan is the plural of wathan, any object worshipped, including stone images and fetishes; it is broader than asnam and includes standing stones and crosses.
rows.anchor: “Evsân” müfredi “vesen” taş vesâireden tapılan herhangi bir şey, fetiş ki “esnâm”dan e‘amdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fabricate falsehood by calling idols gods or intercessors; the idols are merely imagined entities.
rows.anchor: yalan yere onlara mâbud veya

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A portrait of Zayd contains no reality of the living Zayd, only an image of his mortal body; keeping the image and calling it Zayd is a lie.
rows.anchor: Meselâ Zeyd’in resminde bile Zeyd’den bir hakikat yoktur. O resim, bir kıymeti olan canlı Zeyd’in değil, nihâyet toprağa gömülecek ölü bedeninin bir hayâlidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Granting worship to transient imaginings is a grave slander.
rows.anchor: böyle hayâl olan fânîlere mâbud pâyesi vermek ne büyük bühtandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idols cannot provide sustenance; without God's grace they cannot even help someone digest a morsel.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın inâyeti olmayınca meselâ bir lokmacık hazmettiremezler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse from 29:19 through 29:23 is most apparently God's parenthetical address to Muhammad during Ibrahim's story; it could instead be reported as Ibrahim's speech, but the changed verse endings favor the former.
rows.anchor: İbrâhim’e hitab olarak mahkî olmak muhtemil ise de onun kelâmını hikâye sırasında Resûlullah’a hitab olması daha zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the town; the sign left from it is its story or its ruins.
rows.anchor: {ٱلْقَرْيَةِ} bir âyet, bir nişâne

words: ٱتْلُ مَآ أُوحِىَ إِلَيْكَ مِنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı understands the command as sustained, repeated, beautiful recitation of the revealed Book.
rows.anchor: Sen, sana vahyolunan kitabı tilâvet eyle vird ederek devam üzere tekrar tekrar güzel güzel oku.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified command to recite, rather than “recite to them,” tells Muhammad to ignore the unbelievers' provocations and recite in his own sphere while reflecting on prophetic histories and God's signs.
rows.anchor: onun için اُتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ buyurulmamış, mutlak olarak ٱتْلُ buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is to be maintained continually.
rows.anchor: Ve namazı devam üzere kıl

words: إِنَّ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ تَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fahsha means manifest ugliness, indecency, and sexual immorality; munkar means what reason and religious law disapprove, including sin.
rows.anchor: fahşâdan yani açık çirkinlikten, edebsizlikten, fuhşiyyâttan {وَٱلْمُنْكَرِ} ve münkerden: aklın ve şer‘in beğenmeyeceği uygunsuzluktan, masiyetten nehyeder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound prayer, understood and properly performed, also restrains indecency and wrong outside prayer; this restraint is required even if it does not guarantee complete abstention.
rows.anchor: çirkinlikten, uygunsuzluktan nehyeder. Nehiy, intihâyı istilzam etmese bile her hâlde iktizâ eder.

rows.speaker: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that prayer which fails to restrain its worshipper from indecency and wrong only increases that person's distance from God.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den mervîdir ki:

rows.speaker: İbn Mes‘ud
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says that one who does not obey prayer only increases distance from God; obeying it means performing it properly within its limits and upholding its restraint from wrong.
rows.anchor: Onun için İbn Mes‘ud hazretleri demiştir ki: “Namazına itaat etmeyen Allah teâlâ’dan uzaklığı artırmaktan başka bir şey yapmaz.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning in 107:4–5 applies to people who appear to pray but are heedless of prayer's meaning and fail to heed its command.
rows.anchor: فَوَيْلٌۭ لِّلْمُصَلِّينَ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ عَن صَلَاتِهِمْ سَاهُونَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The successful believers are described as humble in prayer, reinforcing the requirement to pray with attention.
rows.anchor: قَدْ أَفْلَحَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِى صَلَاتِهِمْ خَٰشِعُونَ [el-Mü’minûn 23/1-2] buyurulmuştu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer's wisdom and goal are remembrance of God, as 20:14 says; remembering God leads to His remembering the worshipper, as 2:152 states.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Tâhâ’da وَأَقِمِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ لِذِكْرِىٓ [20/14] buyurulduğu vechile namazın hikmeti, gayesi Allah’ın zikridir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is a mi'raj; those who understand this pray with intention and sincerity as though continually meeting their Lord, in light of 2:46.
rows.anchor: Bu suretle namaz bir mi‘râcdır. Bunu bilenler ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُوا۟ رَبِّهِمْ [el-Bakara 2/46]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes God's remembrance as prayer itself, the greatest act, whose essence is remembering God's majesty and presenting human need before Him.
rows.anchor: namaz, haddizâtında en büyük amel

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes prayer the greatest means of restraining indecency and wrong.
rows.anchor: veya fahşâ ve münkerden nehy için en büyük âmildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading is that God's remembrance of the worshipper is greater than the worshipper's remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: Yahut Allah teâlâ’nın sizi anması sizin O’nu anmanızdan daha büyüktür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering that God remembers a person makes them avoid being remembered for even an atom of evil and fills them with good deeds; Elmalılı says this is an even greater force for righteousness.
rows.anchor: ind-i ilâhîde zerre kadar seyyiât ile anılmayı kimse arzu etmeyeceğinden her dem rızâya yükselmek için hiss-i hasenât ile meşbû‘olur. Ve şüphe yok ki bu his, evvelkinden daha büyük bir âmil-i salâh olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To understand this, reflect on how God speaks of Pharaoh and how He speaks of prophets and believers in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: Düşünmeli ki Allah, Kur’ân’ında Firavun gibileri nasıl anıyor, peygamberleri ve mü’minleri nasıl anıyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows everything people do, remembers them accordingly, and requites them accordingly.
rows.anchor: Allah, her ne işlerseniz bilir ona göre anar ve ona göre cezâ verir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged partners are the deities people fabricated and associated with God.
rows.anchor: Allah’a karşı uydurup şirk koştukları mâbudlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For “without pillars you see them,” Elmalılı directs readers to his commentary on 13:2.
rows.anchor: Ra‘d Sûresi’nde ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى رَفَعَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍۢ تَرَوْنَهَا [13/2] âyetinin tefsirine bak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes God's majesty and wisdom to prepare the affirmation of oneness; the shift to first-person speech in “We sent down” and “We gave” serves this purpose.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet, Allah teâlâ’nın izzet ü hikmetini takrir ile tevhîdi temhid ediyor. Ve onun için وَأَنزَلْنَا ile اٰتَيْنَا’da gıyabdan tekellüme iltifat buyuruluyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The listed cosmic and earthly phenomena are God's creation, and the challenge asks what anything worshipped besides Him has created.
rows.anchor: İşte bu zikrolunanlar Allah’ın yarattığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are the polytheists, who wrong the meaning of creation and divinity and depart from manifest truth.
rows.anchor: pek büyük zâlim olan, şirki irtikâb eyleyen müşrikler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They falsely attribute divine creative power to creatures.
rows.anchor: Bir taraftan mahlûka hâlık kudreti isnad ederek “filan şunu yarattı, falan şunu yarattı” diye yalan söylerler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also worship objects known to have created nothing.
rows.anchor: bir taraftan da hiçbir şey yaratmadığı

words: فَأَرُونِى مَاذَا خَلَقَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to the question whether human crafts and inventions count as creation, Elmalılı says wisdom is God's gift, so He is their creator too and deserves thanks; to the wise, shirk is grave injustice.
rows.anchor: hikmetin Allah vergisi olduğu ve binâen‘aleyh hikmet ile yapılan şeylerin de hâlıkı Allah olduğu bilinerek O’na şükredilmesi lâzım geleceği

words: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشْرِكَ بِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even though people are urged to thank their parents, they must not obey them if they pressure them to associate with God; shirk has no basis in knowledge and is impossible.
rows.anchor: anaya babaya dahi şükrü insana tavsiye etmiş olmamızla beraber, onlar seni Bana şirk koşasın diye zorlarlarsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continue to treat unbelieving parents well without joining their sin, meeting their needs, avoiding harshness, caring for them when ill, and arranging their burial after death.
rows.anchor: masiyete iştirak etmeksizin şer‘in râzı olacağı ve kerem ü mürüvvetin iktizâ edeceği vechile sohbetlerinde bulun. Meselâ yemek içmek, giymek gibi ihtiyaçlarını tesviye etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In religious matters, follow the way of sincere monotheists who have turned back to God.
rows.anchor: Bana inâbe etmiş olan hâlis muhlis muvahhidin yolunu tut

words: إِن تَكُ مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍۢ مِّنْ خَرْدَلٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tiny, hidden deed may be good or bad, high or low; God brings it before the person in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: Allah onu getirir âhirette karşına kor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is Latif because His power reaches the finest and most hidden things, and Khabir because His knowledge encompasses them all.
rows.anchor: en ince, en gizli şeylere yetişir {خَبِيرٌۭ} ilmi ile hepsini bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the image of trees as pens and the sea as ink, Elmalılı refers readers to 18:109.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Kehf’te قُل لَّوْ كَانَ ٱلْبَحْرُ [18/109] bak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We forgot you” means God left them in Hell as though forgetting them.
rows.anchor: Çünkü Biz sizi unuttuk yani unutmuş gibi cehennemde bıraktık

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose sides withdraw from beds pray to their Lord with fear and hope by rising at night for tahajjud.
rows.anchor: Rablerine dua ederler gece kalkar teheccüd kılarlar.

rows.speaker: Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
rows.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal relates that, during a journey, the Prophet answered his question about entering Paradise and avoiding Hell with the pillars of worship, then named fasting, charity, and night prayer as good deeds; the author calls the report soundly transmitted and says the Prophet recited 32:16–17.
rows.anchor: Birçokları Mu‘âz b. Cebel radıyallahu anh’tan sahîhan rivayet etmişlerdir ki şöyle demiştir: “Bir seferinde Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem ile beraberdim

words: مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْأَدْنَىٰ دُونَ ٱلْعَذَابِ ٱلْأَكْبَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearer, lesser punishment is worldly punishment; the greater punishment is the punishment of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: “Azâb-ı ednâ”, yakın azab dünya azabı; “azâb-ı ekber” de âhiret azâbıdır.
